Please read all the reviews carefully before taking your pet to Cutler Bay Animal Clinic. They significantly overcharge and add hidden fees that appear on the final bill.

On April 16, 2026, my mother rushed her dog to the clinic early in the morning. The dog was suffering from severe diarrhea and vomiting, had fainted, and was unresponsive.

One positive note is that the staff attended to her quickly. After a few minutes they told her it could take several hours to determine the cause.

The veterinarian then informed my mother that the dog most likely had parvovirus and that there was a chance it could be saved, but emergency treatment would cost about $1,681.56 upfront. In her distress and hoping to save her dog, she paid the full amount.

A few hours later the clinic called to say the dog had died. They immediately informed her that additional services and fees would be charged on top of what she had already paid that day (Roughly $400). Although they ultimately worked with her on those extra charges ($62.50), I found it insensitive and inappropriate that they pushed for more money right after delivering such devastating news.

We believe the clinic may have recognized early on that the dog’s condition was critical and unlikely to improve, yet still presented treatment as a realistic chance of survival.

A responsible veterinarian should clearly explain the severity of the situation and discuss realistic options with the owner before collecting a large payment.

I cannot recommend this clinic. In our experience they gave false hope that the pet could be saved and then charged a very high amount, followed by requests for more money after.

My mother believes this clinic should be investigated for risk of prolonging suffering and financial harm for marginal benefits.

On top of that, their callous approach of making panicked pet owners feel pressured into paying a upfront cost without discussing realistic outcomes or counseling.

There are way to many reviews from other pet owners with similar stories.

I took my 2-month-old puppy to this clinic because she had diarrhea and vomiting. The veterinarian, Ruben Nasio, “if this is he’s real name” saw my puppy. He changed her food and told me to relax, saying she was just a baby. He also sent us home with medicine to stop the symptoms and gave her some injections.
After this visit, my puppy’s condition got worse. I took her to another vet the next day, and they found she was very sick. They put her on fluids and ran tests, which showed she had a parasite called Giardia. They kept her at the clinic with medication and fluids, but unfortunately it was too late, and my puppy passed away a few days later.
I feel that if the first veterinarian had performed the appropriate tests, my puppy might still be here today. Please be cautious before taking your pets to this clinic

Meanwhile it’s September 27, as long as it’s prior to October I think it’s probably ok. They either could tell you that on the phone or not greet you with that information. They charge you for things they don’t provide. They take your dog in back and you never see the veterinarian. I came for a rabies vaccination for two dogs. I asked to actually see the vet since they tried to take my dog in the back. Meanwhile they want to charge you $115 for a dog examination. I asked to have it done in the room so I could see the exam. Another tech gave the tags for the dogs before either were given any sort of shot or care. I don’t even think there is a vet who works there. The only people you see are the techs. After waiting for a half hour, when we asked to have the vet visit removed from the bill, since the vet was busy and to just do the shots. She refused. Then I asked  why did you give me these tags then? A tech tore the tags out of my hand! And asked me how I got those? I said a tech gave them to me. Then I requested my bills which I signed. And they would not return them. Super rude and disappointed!! Be aware. If they are taking your dog in back and not providing the services that you are paying for!

The worst experience I've ever had with my dog's vet here at Cutler Bay Animal Clinic. With or without insurance, the prices are sky-high. Today I took my dog ​​in with vomiting and diarrhea, and the main assistant insisted I buy insurance. She wanted to charge $400 for the blood test alone. Without insurance, it was $200. Anyway, she told me my dog ​​had a pancreatic problem and that the test would come back positive, so I'd have to keep her on fluids and metronidazole for at least two days for pancreatitis. The whole thing was going to cost me a whopping $1200, without medication. That woman was crazy! I went to another clinic, and the blood tests were all fine. The CPL test for the pancreas was negative, and they showed me the results (all with proof). In total, the same tests, including the three medications, cost me $380. Outrageous! Scammers, and they don't offer payment options. I definitely don't recommend them.
